text:
sanjay: Heads-up — Zenwell legal asked for a per-org routing exception so requests using their tokens always prefer the LTS-quantized model for cost predictability. They want this scoped to the org (not an account-wide global flag). Is this something we can support without adding a messy global allowlist?
karla: We can. Two immediate questions: precedence (does org override beat smart routing?) and how we surface this in the console. Also: telemetry and billing implications. :thinking_face: 
evan: Product context — Zenwell is enterprise, willing to pay for committed capacity. Their ask: stable latency & predictable cost, not absolute SOTA quality. They want a simple checkbox in the console and an API toggle for SEs. Also need an audit entry for legal.
karla: Implementation options we discussed off-thread: 
  1) soft override — set routing_preference: "prefer_lts". Gateway tries LTS first but will fallback to higher-tier variant if LTS is unavailable. Safer for availability.
  2) hard pin — exact model id route. No fallback. Predictable but brittle and can cause capacity hot spots.
nana: SRE note — hard pins are dangerous at scale. If many enterprises pin the same model we can overwhelm the pool or block autoscaler decisions. We need per-org pin quotas + preflight capacity checks and alerts on pin saturation.
karla: Also need TTL on exceptions and revocation workflow. Legal asked for 12-month pin with manual revoke. We should avoid permanent pins.
sanjay: Requirement: every org override must generate an audit log entry with actor, reason, TTL, and a revocation token for SEs. Zenwell specifically also wants a denylist preventing gov-certified models from being used by their traffic — so dual allow/deny semantics.
karla: Proposed internal API payload (gateway rule):
```yaml
match:
  org_id: "org_zenwell"
  token_scope: "production"
action:
  type: "route_override"
  mode: "prefer_lts" # or "pin_exact"
  model_id: "redwood/lts-v1-q4"
meta:
  ttl: "365d"
  created_by: "sanjay"
  reason: "Cost predictability (legal)"
  audit_id: "audit_2026_00123"
```
karla: Gateway changes needed: header injection (x-org-override-id), precedence rules (org override > routing policy unless soft flag set), and clear failure semantics (what happens on model unavailable). Also console needs UI to show override source and allow revoke.
evan: Console UX: show an "Override source" badge, cost-delta estimate, and a link to the audit log entry. Only org admins + SEs should be able to toggle. When soft override is active, show a tooltip: "Fallback allowed — may route to higher-tier models on failure."
nana: Telemetry: tag requests with `x-routing-source: org-override/zenwell` and an `override_mode` dimension. Ensure this flows into per-route latency/cost dashboards and quota counters. We should also add alerting for "override hit rate" drops (if LTS becomes unavailable).
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: gateway:route-override-service v0.9 -> canary (5%) scheduled in 10m.
karla: I'll draft the PR for gateway + console changes. Plan: implement soft override first, add quota enforcement and TTL, then consider hard pins behind an ops-only feature flag.
sanjay: I'll own the audit retention policy and coordinate with security on denylist definitions.
evan: SGTM. Let's sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to align SLOs, console copy, and rollout plan. @karla @ana @sanjay
karla: Cool — opening issues and a brief design doc now. :white_check_mark:
